review_reference: Owner decisions of 18 Nov 2026 on hid-system#258 (Akos EHR plan, Release A, lane D): ORD-2 'activated prescriptions go automatically to the hospital's own pharmacy: YES' and 'pharmacy and lab staff get their own facility's work items only, never the chart'; Q102 'a fictional QA pharmacist and lab worker at QA Hospital, sealed QA only' (QA-1). Contract: docs/INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md, the 0133 and 0134 sections. This branch's own declaration, for its own checks: it names exactly 0133, 0134 and runtime-grants.sql. The hand-over on #258 (Rahman integrates 0128-0137) replaces it with one combined declaration for that release. To be signed by the owner.
evidence: DRAFT, not signed: the owner's review and signature are still to come, and the release integrator (#258) replaces this branch's declaration with one combined declaration for 0128-0137 (exactly those files plus the merged runtime-grants.sql, with its new sha256). Migrations 0133_own_facility_pharmacy_and_lab_work.sql (sha256 95be046cbd51022981d71d5ff8b8081db15b3f9e2051a166a17d3767218aeae8) and 0134_sealed_qa_hospital_pharmacy_lab_staff.sql (sha256 13a58405e179befac7eb3e1854862b33787e040177a48fa98f55557b2cedb5b7) and their runtime-grants.sql block (file sha256 213bfc253a6c4d21d163bb561090f37be1d8fba14072bcb6f85afddb7ee4f225; it grants the two halves of the own-work member test to the Lab and Pharmacy runtimes, ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed to the EHR runtime, and revokes the withdrawal trigger function from PUBLIC). WHAT 0133 DOES: the own-work member test, in two halves: identity.facility_work_session_membership (direct care, the session's facility, <kind>.work-item.read and <kind>.order-route.receive held there through an active membership, which today only the pharmacist and lab roles hold; it answers that membership, or null) and identity.facility_work_patient_allows (STRICT, given that membership: still the session's, at the row's facility, active and not on hold, of an active account whose subject is the session's actor; the patient active; no deny directive covering that member), and whole as identity.facility_work_member_allows; called on its own by the Lab or Pharmacy runtime, the row's half answers for an active account's own membership row (active, not on hold) whatever its roles, staff record, facility or organization, and for the sealed logins whose ids are public (0098's demo login once its owner has reset it, 0123's QA logins): whether a patient id the caller holds is active and whether a deny directive covers that member (whether to close that with an owner-only list of the patients with own work at each facility is an owner question on #280); the work items gain a read policy for own items (no order route), and the work chain 42 policies decided item by item, the path to the own work item read in the policy itself by the querying role: 44 permissive policies named staff_own_work_*, which sort after every lab_* and pharmacy_* policy, so PostgreSQL (which joins permissive policies with OR in reverse name order) asks them first; each asks the session's half once per statement (one InitPlan) and, for every other session, never calls the row's half or reads the path; 0124's patient cards gain the test; 0086's context_allows and work_item_allows are unchanged, so the imported evidence, the Lab outbox and the route reports gain nothing and a route-backed item's rows never pass; pharmacy.own_prescription_sends (row-level security on, no policy, no grant); ehr.send_prescription_to_own_pharmacy for the EHR runtime (pharmacy-api's own PharmacyWorkItemCreated payload; after a dispensing it answers that the pharmacy already has the prescription) and ehr.own_pharmacy_staffed (its no_pharmacy test alone, read only, for the prescription list and page; it asks the full permission check of pharmacy staff only); the withdrawal: a trigger on ehr.prescriptions (prescriptions_own_pharmacy_send_withdrawn, its SECURITY DEFINER function the owner's alone) records a sent prescription held, cancelled, entered in error, edited or resumed whichever ehr-api image changes it, and ehr.withdraw_own_pharmacy_send and the pharmacy list's states report it only while the item is not dispensed; the own-work access check answers the audit basis (consent for a member holding its own grant for the action, else own-work, as the list's reader does); two ehr.prescriptions policies for the dispensing validator's owner only. UNDO (by hand only, in one transaction): drop the withdrawal trigger, its function and the three other readers of the sends table before the table, or every later prescription status or version change fails (42P01); D1's two halves go last; 0133's header gives the order. WHAT 0134 DOES: where 0123 installed the sealed QA tenant (Amazon RDS: production and staging) the QA Pharmacist and QA Lab Scientist logins gain a pharmacist and a lab membership at QA Hospital; a login that is not 0123's now, or one the QA Facility Admin already gave that role at QA Hospital (active or not), is left alone with a notice instead of stopping the release; elsewhere nothing. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's images call none of the new functions; through the changed policies today's lab-api and pharmacy-api list the facility's own items for its pharmacy and lab staff and record them as 0124 did (with OWN_WORK_PATIENT_CARD_ENABLED on, a per-patient row with basis consent even for a member without a grant; off, the default and production's setting, the collection row only) until the new images serve: deploy them with 0133 (whether they should go out in the same window, and whether a rollback of one alone may stand after it, is with the owner as part of Q114-Q120); a single item, a dispensing and every chain command still ask Identity's consent in today's images; the withdrawal is the database's, so today's ehr-api images mark it too; ehr-api answers ownPharmacyStaffed and pharmacyHandoff only where 0133 is applied. LOCKS: 0133 takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.prescriptions, lab.work_items, pharmacy.work_items and the 20 chain tables that gain a policy (and ACCESS SHARE on the four identity tables and auth.accounts, which its SQL functions read; 28 tables) NOWAIT; first in its transaction (the runner applies each file in its own) it retries every 100 ms for at most 5 s, else 55P03 with nothing of 0133 applied; when its transaction already holds another migration's table locks (the runner's dry run of 0128-0137 in one transaction) it makes one attempt and no sleep; in that dry run the locks of every file last until it ends, so every Lab and Pharmacy work list and chain read waits meanwhile, and a later file that waits for its own locks (0136's plain LOCK TABLE of auth.permissions, auth.role_permissions and identity.access_requests, up to the runner's 5 s lock_timeout) keeps them held, which the combined declaration must state (the dry run belongs in a quiet window). 0134 writes at most two rows in each of two tables, only where the QA tenant is installed. COST: lab-api's work list for a busy laboratory (1,050 work items, the database-migration job's runtime check, which runs with a superuser owner): 7.7-8.4 s for the consent-backed clinician (0001-0127: 7.2 s, the same 5,631 consent checks) and 1.3-1.5 s for the lab scientist without a grant, the same 200 rows, under lab-api's 15 s limit; auth.membership_has_permission 16 and 74 times per statement. With every table and function owned by a non-superuser role, as in production: a pharmacy's list of 3,501 items 0.5 s for its pharmacist; a laboratory's 2.1 s at 2,000 lab work items and 3.6-3.8 s at 4,000 for its lab scientist (the list reads the laboratory's whole history; from about 5,000 items PostgreSQL's JIT adds about 3.4 s, because the own-work policies raise the list's estimated cost about 40 times; about 15,000 items reach the limit with jit on, PostgreSQL's default, about 19,000 with jit off); the consent-backed clinician's 12.7-14.2 s at 2,000 (0001-0127: 12.4-13.7 s; JIT now compiles it, about 0.3 s; 0086's consent test on every row of that history reaches the limit at about 2,200 items whatever 0133 does, an owner question on #280); a lab result's verification insert 0.16 s. The first form of the own-work policies (a chain function asking the whole test on every row, d724af0c) took 22 s and 19 s on that busy laboratory and failed the job (57014). PROVED (local, throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15, synthetic data, at PROOF_HEAD; the commit after it changes only this evidence): the TUF staging rehearsal passed (4 min 13 s; 0028 -> 0134 upgrade, 599 foreign keys, 0 orphans, restore equal; order_routes, records_processing, own_work_patient_cards, prescription_details and own_facility_work runtime checks pass through the booted services as their exact runtime roles); a fresh install of 0001-0127 + 0133 + 0134 as a superuser and as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (plan, dry run rolled back, apply, bootstrap, verify-only, 0 pending); all 102 database suites pass on the superuser build and 100 of 102 on the NOBYPASSRLS build (schema's job_events case and records-processing-draft case 6n, which fail the same way on staging 1f5e2c2a itself), on an ICU en-US cluster too; on staging 1f5e2c2a's 128 files applied by its own runner as the NOBYPASSRLS migrator the plan is exactly [0133, 0134], the dry run rolls back with privileges unchanged, the apply takes 423 ms (0133 134 ms), a second run answers 'already applied', the release adds exactly 31 EXECUTE grants and removes none, this branch's runtime-grants.sql changes nothing after it, and the suites answer 100 of 102 as on staging; the refusals answer their own messages (each missing marker, a missing column, a changed or missing relied-on body, a table of another owner, non-owner appliers, a hid_ role that is the owner's member, 0134 without 0133), nothing applied; behind a conflicting lock on each of the 28 tables 0133 stops after 5.1-5.2 s with 55P03 while writers finish in 10-14 ms, and behind a 2 s reader it retries and applies; with another migration's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE already held in the same transaction it stops in 28 ms and a consent_grants reader waits 10 ms; 0134 applies with an administrator's active or deactivated pharmacist membership of the QA Pharmacist at QA Hospital and with a deleted QA login; db:test-staging-upgrade passes with staging 1f5e2c2a's runtime-grants.sql as the baseline; scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs passes (130 migrations); ehr-api, pharmacy-api and lab-api typecheck and their jest tests pass (1517 with 13 skipped, 303, 633); the release tests pass but for the three that stop at 'components config.migration.files: missing migration prefix' while 0128-0132 are not on staging; the database-migration job's runtime check (test-patient-evidence-runtime.mjs) passes on an ICU en-US PostgreSQL 16 with the lab scientist's read added (1.3-1.5 s, 74 permission checks per statement). Independent adversarial review after each round (five so far), the last three of the session-once policies: a statement that changes its session settings partway reads nothing more, on the Lab and Pharmacy work items and a chain table of each (suite case 7g, each probe failing on an unbound row's half whatever the statistics), only the session's own member of the facility's pharmacy or lab staff reads own work through the policies, the row's half asks on each row only what a statement can change, and the Pharmacy policies are asked first (case 7g compares the consent checks; section 8 holds the name order). TO COMPLETE: the owner's review and signature (reviewed_by); the owner's answers on #280 (Q114-Q120: routing elsewhere after the automatic send, the image order and single-image rollbacks with 0133; whether a change after a dispensing should reach the pharmacy); the coordinator's answers recorded: OWN_WORK_PATIENT_CARD_ENABLED is off in production, a NOTICE is enough for an existing QA Hospital membership, and the per-file apply is acceptable if today's images are checked between files in the integration rehearsal; and the combined declaration above, whose integrator re-checks that 0128-0132 neither replace work_item_allows nor lock the two work item tables. COLLATION: 0133's post-checks compare its sends table's constraint and index lists and the own-work policies' names in a fixed order (COLLATE "C"), so they hold whatever the database's default collation is; proved by applying 0001-0127, 0133 and 0134 as a superuser with MIGRATION_TARGET=rds (as the database-migration image test does) on a cluster whose default collation is ICU en-US, like the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image's en_US.utf8, where every post-check passes and every database suite (17 + 85) passes.
